revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Wiring the Studio
revealWordProblem.text: A recording studio runs cables for its microphones. The cost of wiring one room is the expression 5x + 7 + 3x + 2, where x is the number of microphones in that room. Write the cost as a simplified expression by combining like terms. Then find the total cost when the room has x = 4 microphones.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Combine like terms: 5x + 3x = 8x and 7 + 2 = 9, so the simplified expression is 8x + 9. When x = 4, the cost is 8(4) + 9 = 32 + 9 = 41 dollars.

vocabulary.definition: Rewrite an expression in a shorter equivalent form by combining like terms and using properties.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una expresión en una forma equivalente más corta combinando términos semejantes y usando propiedades.
vocabulary.cloze: Combine ___ ___ to write a shorter expression with the same value.

examples.why: The 4 has no x and cannot join.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.
vocabulary.visual: 5x and 3x are like terms (both x); 5x and 5y are NOT (different variables); 2x and 2x² are NOT (different powers)
vocabulary.cloze: Terms with the same variable part, like 3y and 8y, are ___.

examples.why: They share the same variable y.
They have different variables, so they are not like terms.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar o restar términos con la misma letra en uno solo.
vocabulary.visual: 8m + 3m = 11m — add the coefficients (8 + 3 = 11) and keep the variable (m)
vocabulary.cloze: To add or subtract like terms into a single term is to ___ them.

examples.why: A constant cannot join a variable term.

vocabulary.definition: To rewrite an expression in a shorter form that is still equal to the original.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una expresión en una forma más corta que sigue siendo igual a la original.
vocabulary.visual: 2a + 5a + 3 simplifies to 7a + 3 — the two a-terms combine, the constant stays
vocabulary.cloze: Rewriting an expression in a shorter form that is still equal to it is to ___ it.

examples.why: Like terms combine; the constant stays.
The 3 is a constant, not an a-term.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número frente a una letra, como el 3 en 3x.
vocabulary.visual: In 9x, the coefficient is 9 — it tells you 'nine groups of x'; if x = 2, then 9x = 18

vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número, variable o producto de ellos, separado por signos + o −.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do we simplify by combining like terms?
conceptIntro.intro: Like terms are terms with the same variable, like 2x and 5x. To simplify an expression, you add or subtract the like terms to make it shorter. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Only combine terms that have the same variable part; numbers without a variable combine with each other.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The rooms need microphones and stands: (4 + 2 + 6) microphones and (3 + 5 + 1) stands.
Microphones are like items, so I add: 4 + 2 + 6 = 12 microphones.
Stands are like items, so I add: 3 + 5 + 1 = 9 stands.
In algebra this is the same as 4m + 2m + 6m + 3s + 5s + 1s = 12m + 9s.
linesEs: Los salones necesitan micrófonos y atriles: (4 + 2 + 6) micrófonos y (3 + 5 + 1) atriles.
Los micrófonos son cosas semejantes, así que sumo: 4 + 2 + 6 = 12 micrófonos.
Los atriles son cosas semejantes, así que sumo: 3 + 5 + 1 = 9 atriles.
En álgebra esto es lo mismo que 4m + 2m + 6m + 3a + 5a + 1a = 12m + 9a.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's simplify 5x + 3x. Are these like terms?
Yes, both have x, so we add the numbers in front: 5 + 3 = 8.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: Sí, los dos tienen x, así que sumamos los números de adelante: 5 + 3 = 8.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.

linesEs: Intenta los problemas de práctica de abajo. El botón de pistas está ahí cuando te atores — úsalo, eso es ser listo.
Recuerda la idea clave: Combina solo los términos que tienen la misma parte variable; los números sin variable se combinan entre sí.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Construyámoslo juntos — ¿Cómo simplificamos combinando términos semejantes?
conceptIntro.introEs: Los términos semejantes son términos con la misma variable, como 2x y 5x. Para simplificar una expresión, sumas o restas los términos semejantes para hacerla más corta. Veremos un ejemplo resuelto, haremos uno juntos y luego harás algunos con pistas disponibles cuando las necesites.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Combina solo los términos que tienen la misma parte variable; los números sin variable se combinan entre sí.

explore.instructions: Quick warm-up together: Identify the like terms in each expression. Group the terms that can be combined.

discourse.prompt: What rule determines whether two terms are 'like terms'? Why can't you combine unlike terms?
discourse.sentenceFrame: Two terms are like terms when they have the same ___. You cannot combine ___ and ___ because they represent different ___.

choiceFeedback: 7x and 3x are like terms. 7 + 3 = 10. Result: 10x.
Did you multiply 7 × 3? Add the coefficients: 7 + 3 = 10.
Same variable x: add the coefficients 7 + 3 = 10.
hints: 7x and 3x have the same variable x, so they're like terms and can combine.
Add the coefficients; the x stays exactly the same — no squaring, no multiplying coefficients.
Compute 7 + 3 and place that sum in front of x.
hintsEs: 7x y 3x tienen la misma variable x, así que son términos semejantes y se pueden combinar.
Suma los coeficientes; la x se queda exactamente igual: no se eleva al cuadrado ni se multiplican los coeficientes.
Calcula 7 + 3 y pon esa suma delante de x.

approaching.explanation: 9n + 2n = 11n. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 11n + 4.
choiceFeedback: 9n and 2n are like terms: 9 + 2 = 11. Keep 4 separate.
4 is a constant term; 11n is the combined variable term.
You stuck the digits 9 and 2 together instead of adding them. Like terms are combined by adding the coefficients: 9 + 2.
hints: There are two n-terms (9n and 2n) and one lonely constant (4) with no partner.
Combine only the like terms; the constant 4 stays separate in your answer.
Add 9n + 2n by adding 9 + 2. The 4 keeps its own spot at the end.
approaching.explanationEs: 9n + 2n = 11n. La constante 4 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 11n + 4.
hintsEs: Hay dos términos con n (9n y 2n) y una constante solitaria (4) sin pareja.
Combina solo los términos semejantes; la constante 4 se queda aparte en tu respuesta.
Suma 9n + 2n sumando 9 + 2. El 4 conserva su propio lugar al final.

approaching.explanation: 6x and 2x are like terms because they both have the same variable (x) raised to the same power (1).
choiceFeedback: Like terms have the same variable raised to the same power.
6x and 6y have different variables, so they're not like terms.
x and x² are different (different powers), so not like terms.
hints: Like terms need the exact same variable raised to the exact same power.
Compare two things in each pair: the letter itself and the small exponent on it. Both must match exactly.
Check each pair in order: same letter, and the same small exponent on it? Both must match.
approaching.explanationEs: 6x y 2x son términos semejantes porque los dos tienen la misma variable (x) elevada a la misma potencia (1).
hintsEs: Los términos semejantes necesitan exactamente la misma variable elevada exactamente a la misma potencia.
Compara dos cosas en cada pareja: la letra y el pequeño exponente sobre ella. Ambos deben coincidir exactamente.
Prueba la primera pareja: 6x y 2x — ¿misma letra? ¿misma potencia? Si ambas coinciden, son semejantes.

choiceFeedback: 5a and 2a are like terms: 5 + 2 = 7. Keep 3 separate.
Did you add all numbers? Like terms: 5a + 2a = 7a. Constant: 3.
You glued the digits 5 and 2 together instead of adding them. Add the coefficients of the like terms: 5 + 2.
hints: Spot the like terms: 5a and 2a share the variable a. The 3 has no variable.
Combine the a-terms by adding their coefficients; carry the 3 along unchanged.
Add 5 + 2 for the a coefficient, then write the constant 3 after it.
hintsEs: Identifica los términos semejantes: 5a y 2a comparten la variable a. El 3 no tiene variable.
Combina los términos con a sumando sus coeficientes; el 3 se lleva sin cambios.
Suma 5 + 2 para el coeficiente de a y luego escribe la constante 3 después.

approaching.instructions: Sort each pair of terms by whether they are like terms (can be combined) or not.
hints: Like terms match in BOTH the variable letter and its exponent. Plain numbers only pair with plain numbers.
For each card ask two questions: same letter? Same power? Two yes answers = like terms.
First card: 4m and 7m — both use m to the first power, so they can combine. Place it, then quiz the next pair.
approaching.explanation: Terms are alike only when the variable AND its exponent match: 4m and 7m, 5n and n, and 6a and 9a all pass that test. The pairs 3x and 3y use different letters, 8 and 2p pair a constant with a variable term, and 2x² and 2x use different exponents, so none of those can be combined.
approaching.explanationEs: Los términos son semejantes solo cuando coinciden la variable Y su exponente: 4m y 7m, 5n y n, y 6a y 9a pasan esa prueba. Los pares 3x y 3y usan letras distintas, 8 y 2p juntan una constante con un término con variable, y 2x² y 2x usan exponentes distintos, así que ninguno de esos se puede combinar.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada pareja de términos según si son términos semejantes (se pueden combinar) o no.
hintsEs: Los términos semejantes coinciden TANTO en la letra como en el exponente. Los números simples solo se juntan con números simples.
En cada tarjeta hazte dos preguntas: ¿misma letra? ¿misma potencia? Dos síes = términos semejantes.
Primera tarjeta: 4m y 7m — ambos usan m a la primera potencia, así que se pueden combinar. Colócala y evalúa la siguiente pareja.

approaching.instructions: Simplify each expression by combining like terms.
hints: Row 1 shows the move: gather the matching variable terms first, then bring the constant along.
For each row, underline the variable terms and circle the constants. Combine each group separately.
Row 2: 6x + 4 + 2x + 7 — pair 6x with 2x, and 4 with 7. Add each pair, then write both parts.
approaching.explanation: In each row you combine the variable terms and the constants separately: 3a + 5a = 8a leaves 8a + 2; 6x + 2x = 8x with 4 + 7 = 11 gives 8x + 11; 10m − 3m = 7m gives 7m + 5; and 4y + y = 5y with 3 + 9 = 12 gives 5y + 12. The constants never merge with the variable terms because they have no variable.
approaching.explanationEs: En cada fila combinas por separado los términos con variable y las constantes: 3a + 5a = 8a deja 8a + 2; 6x + 2x = 8x con 4 + 7 = 11 da 8x + 11; 10m − 3m = 7m da 7m + 5; y 4y + y = 5y con 3 + 9 = 12 da 5y + 12. Las constantes nunca se unen con los términos con variable porque no tienen variable.
approaching.instructionsEs: Simplifica cada expresión combinando los términos semejantes.
hintsEs: La fila 1 muestra el movimiento: junta primero los términos con la misma variable y luego lleva la constante.
Para cada fila, subraya los términos con variable y encierra las constantes. Combina cada grupo por separado.
Fila 2: 6x + 4 + 2x + 7 — junta 6x con 2x, y 4 con 7. Suma cada pareja y luego escribe ambas partes.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake — Exponent Slip
onLevel.correctWork: 4x and 3x are like terms, so add the coefficients 4 + 3 = 7 and KEEP the variable exactly as it is: the answer is 7x, not 7x². Adding like terms never changes the exponent on the variable. (Check: at x = 2, 4x + 3x = 8 + 6 = 14, and 7x = 14, but 7x² = 28.)
hints: When you add like terms, does the little exponent on x change?
4x + 3x means 7 groups of x, which is 7x. The exponent stays at 1.
onLevel.titleEs: Descubre el error — resbalón con el exponente
onLevel.explanation: Adding the coefficients 4 + 3 = 7 was right, but the Simplify step also changed x into x². Combining like terms only counts how many x's you have, so 4x + 3x = 7x — check it at x = 2, where 8 + 6 = 14 matches 7x but not 7x² = 28.
onLevel.explanationEs: Sumar los coeficientes 4 + 3 = 7 estuvo bien, pero el paso de simplificar también cambió x por x². Combinar términos semejantes solo cuenta cuántas x tienes, así que 4x + 3x = 7x; compruébalo con x = 2, donde 8 + 6 = 14 coincide con 7x pero no con 7x² = 28.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 4x y 3x son términos semejantes, así que suma los coeficientes 4 + 3 = 7 y CONSERVA la variable tal como está: la respuesta es 7x, no 7x². Sumar términos semejantes nunca cambia el exponente de la variable. (Comprueba: en x = 2, 4x + 3x = 8 + 6 = 14, y 7x = 14, pero 7x² = 28.)
hintsEs: Cuando sumas términos semejantes, ¿cambia el exponente pequeño de la x?
4x + 3x significa 7 grupos de x, o sea 7x. El exponente sigue siendo 1.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake — Swept-Up Constant
onLevel.correctWork: The 4 is a constant with no variable, so it cannot be combined with the x-terms. Combine only the like terms: 6x + 2x = 8x, and the 4 stays on its own. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4. (Check: at x = 1, 6x + 4 + 2x = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, and 8x + 4 = 12, but 12x = 12 only by accident — at x = 2 it gives 24 instead of the true 20.)
hints: Is 4 a like term with 6x and 2x? It has no variable, so it cannot join them.
Combine the x-terms first (6x + 2x = 8x), then write the leftover constant: 8x + 4.
onLevel.titleEs: Descubre el error — la constante arrastrada
onLevel.explanation: The Combine step swept the constant 4 in with the coefficients 6 and 2, but 4 has no variable, so it is not a like term. Only 6x + 2x = 8x combine, and the 4 stays on its own, giving 8x + 4 — at x = 2 that is 20, while 12x would give 24.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de combinar arrastró la constante 4 junto con los coeficientes 6 y 2, pero el 4 no tiene variable, así que no es un término semejante. Solo se combinan 6x + 2x = 8x, y el 4 se queda aparte, lo que da 8x + 4; con x = 2 eso es 20, mientras que 12x daría 24.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El 4 es una constante sin variable, así que no puede combinarse con los términos con x. Combina solo los términos semejantes: 6x + 2x = 8x, y el 4 se queda solo. La expresión simplificada correcta es 8x + 4. (Comprueba: en x = 1, 6x + 4 + 2x = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12, y 8x + 4 = 12, pero 12x = 12 solo por casualidad — en x = 2 da 24 en lugar del verdadero 20.)
hintsEs: ¿4 es un término semejante a 6x y 2x? No tiene variable, así que no puede unirse a ellos.
Combina primero los términos con x (6x + 2x = 8x), luego escribe la constante que sobra: 8x + 4.

onLevel.stem: The board shows 3x + 5x on one channel. Simplify it.
onLevel.explanation: 3x and 5x are like terms, so add the coefficients: 3 + 5 = 8. The variable x stays, giving 8x.
choiceFeedback: 3x and 5x are like terms. Add the coefficients: 3 + 5 = 8. Result: 8x.
Did you multiply 3 × 5? You're adding like terms, not multiplying.
Both have x, so combine: 3x + 5x = 8x.
onLevel.stemEs: El tablero muestra 3x + 5x en un canal. Simplifícalo.
onLevel.explanationEs: 3x y 5x son términos semejantes, así que suma los coeficientes: 3 + 5 = 8. La variable x se queda, lo que da 8x.
hints: Like terms have exactly the same variable part, so 3x and 5x can be combined.
Add the numbers in front of the variable and keep the variable itself unchanged.
The coefficients here are 3 and 5. Add those two numbers, then attach the x to your result.
hintsEs: Los términos semejantes tienen exactamente la misma parte variable, así que 3x y 5x se pueden combinar.
Suma los números que están delante de la variable y deja la variable igual.
Aquí los coeficientes son 3 y 5. Suma esos dos números y luego pega la x a tu resultado.

onLevel.explanation: 4a + a = 5a (remember a means 1a). The 2 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 5a + 2.
choiceFeedback: 4a and a are like terms: 4a + a = 5a. Keep the 2 separate.
Adding like terms does not create a new exponent. 4a + a still has a to the first power.
It looks like you combined the 2 with the terms that have a. The 2 has no variable, so it is not a like term with 4a or a.
onLevel.explanationEs: 4a + a = 5a (recuerda que a significa 1a). El 2 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 5a + 2.
hints: Only terms with the same variable can be combined; a plain number stays on its own.
Remember that a by itself means 1a, so line it up with the 4a.
Add the coefficients of 4a and 1a, and leave the 2 exactly where it is.
hintsEs: Solo se pueden combinar los términos con la misma variable; un número solo se queda aparte.
Recuerda que a sola significa 1a, así que alinéala con 4a.
Suma los coeficientes de 4a y 1a, y deja el 2 exactamente donde está.

onLevel.explanation: Subtract the coefficients of the like terms: 7 − 3 = 4. Keep the variable y, giving 4y.
choiceFeedback: 7y and 3y are like terms. 7y − 3y = 4y.
Subtract the coefficients: 7 − 3 = 4. The variable stays y.
Combine: 7y minus 3y gives 4y.
onLevel.explanationEs: Resta los coeficientes de los términos semejantes: 7 − 3 = 4. Conserva la variable y, lo que da 4y.
hints: 7y and 3y are like terms because they share the same variable y.
Subtract the coefficients and keep the variable attached to your answer.
The coefficients are 7 and 3. Subtract them, then write the y back onto the result.
hintsEs: 7y y 3y son términos semejantes porque comparten la misma variable y.
Resta los coeficientes y mantén la variable pegada a tu respuesta.
Los coeficientes son 7 y 3. Réstalos y luego vuelve a escribir la y en el resultado.

onLevel.explanation: 6m + 3m = 9m. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 9m + 4.
choiceFeedback: 6m and 3m are like terms: 6m + 3m = 9m. Keep 4 separate.
Did you combine 9 + 4? Like terms are 6m and 3m. Constants stay separate.
It looks like you added the 4 in with the terms that have m. The 4 has no variable, so it cannot be combined with 6m or 3m.
onLevel.explanationEs: 6m + 3m = 9m. La constante 4 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 9m + 4.
hints: Sort the expression first: which terms carry an m, and which one is just a number?
Combine only the m terms; the constant has no partner, so it stays as it is.
Add the coefficients 6 and 3 to build the m term, then write the + 4 after it.
hintsEs: Primero clasifica la expresión: ¿cuáles términos llevan m y cuál es solo un número?
Combina únicamente los términos con m; la constante no tiene pareja, así que se queda igual.
Suma los coeficientes 6 y 3 para armar el término con m y luego escribe el + 4 después.

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is 9m + 4. 6m + 3m = 9m. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 9m + 4.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es 9m + 4. 6m + 3m = 9m. La constante 4 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 9m + 4.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Simplify Algebraic Expressions is sweeping a constant into the variable terms — for example, simplifying 6x + 4 + 2x as 12x by adding all three numbers (6 + 4 + 2 = 12) instead of recognizing that 4 has no variable and cannot combine with 6x and 2x. The correct simplified expression is 8x + 4 (combine 6x + 2x = 8x, and let the 4 stay on its own). Before you submit, check that every term you combined has the exact same variable part.

connect.scenario: A music festival needs supplies for 3 stages. Stage 1 needs 8m + 5 cables, Stage 2 needs 3m + 7 cables, and Stage 3 needs 4m + 2 cables, where m represents the number of microphones per stage. The total order is (8m + 5) + (3m + 7) + (4m + 2).
connect.promptQuestion: Simplify the total order expression. What does each part of the simplified expression tell you?
connect.prompt: The total order simplifies to ___m + ___. The ___ tells us ___ and the ___ tells us ___.

check.explanation: Add the m-terms: 8m + 3m + 4m = 15m. Add the constants: 5 + 7 + 2 = 14. 15m and 14 are unlike terms, so they cannot be combined.

check.stem: What does the 15m tell the festival?
choices: 15 cables are needed for every microphone
check.explanation: 15 is the coefficient of m, so for each microphone the festival needs 15 cables across all three stages.

check.stem: If each stage has 4 microphones (m = 4), how many cables in total?

connect.modelAnswer: (8m + 5) + (3m + 7) + (4m + 2) = 15m + 14. The 15m says 15 cables are needed for every microphone, and the 14 is the fixed number of extra cables needed no matter how many microphones there are. With m = 4, that is 15(4) + 14 = 74 cables.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Simplify 6x + 3 + 2x + 5.
exitTicket.explanation: 6x + 2x = 8x and 3 + 5 = 8, so the simplified expression is 8x + 8.
choiceFeedback: Adding 6x + 2x adds the coefficients — the exponent doesn't change. It stays 8x, not 8x².
The digits were pushed together. Combine like terms by adding: 6x + 2x = 8x and 3 + 5 = 8.
16x folds ALL the numbers into the x-term. Only 6x and 2x are like terms; 3 + 5 = 8 stays a constant.
hints: Find the two families: x-terms (6x and 2x) and constants (3 and 5). Only family members combine.
Add the x coefficients together, add the constants together, and keep the variable's power unchanged.
Start with 6x + 2x — add 6 + 2. Then combine 3 + 5 for the constant part.

questions.explanation: Multiply the 5 by each term inside: 5 × x = 5x and 5 × 3 = 15.

questions.stem: Which shows 6n + 18 factored using its GREATEST common factor?
questions.explanation: Check each option first. 6(n + 3), 3(2n + 6) and 2(3n + 9) all equal 6n + 18. So all three are correct factorings. But the question asks for the GREATEST common factor, and the GCF of 6 and 18 is 6.
